data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without induction because it is a pragmatic wager, not an epistemic probability claim: choosing the theory that has survived severe tests is the only rational choice available if we must act, as it has demonstrated a capacity to withstand falsification that others lack.","counterconditions":[{"case":"refuted if it can be demonstrated that preferring the better-corroborated theory logically entails an assumption that the future will resemble the past, thereby making the 'pragmatic wager' indistinguishable from the inductive principle Popper explicitly rejects","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if the analogy of betting on a horse fails because scientific theories face an unknown reality where surviving tests demonstrates no positive 'fitness'","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if the phrase 'educated guesswork' is a contradiction in terms within a strictly non-inductive framework, rendering the preference an arbitrary psychological habit","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Past success guarantees nothing about the future (rejecting induction), but the theory surviving severest tests proves its 'fitness' in the specific environment of reality so far; choosing it is akin to betting on the horse that has won every race\u2014we do not know it will win the next, but it is the only rational bet.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
